# Web/Frontend for Backend Engineers ## SSR vs CSR ``` SSR (Server-Side Rendering): 1. Request: GET /home 2. Server: render HTML with data 3. Response: Welcome, John 4. Browser: display (fast, searchable) Pros: ✓ Fast first load, SEO, no JS errors Cons: ✗ Every request hits server, slower updates CSR (Client-Side Rendering): 1. Request: GET /home 2. Server: returns empty HTML + app.js 3. Browser: downloads app.js (React, Vue, etc.) 4. JavaScript: fetches /api/user, renders HTML 5. Display: slower, but interactive Pros: ✓ Rich interactivity, fast subsequent updates Cons: ✗ Slow first load, SEO harder, JS required Hybrid (Next.js, Remix): ├─ SSR: initial load server-rendered ├─ Hydration: JavaScript takes over ├─ Best of both: fast + interactive └─ Recommended for modern apps ``` ## Core Web Vitals ``` Metrics Google cares about: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint): ├─ Time to paint largest element (image, text) ├─ Target: <2.5 seconds ├─ Impact: image optimization, server response time FID (First Input Delay): ├─ Time from click to response ├─ Target: <100ms ├─ Impact: JavaScript blocking (remove unused JS) CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift): ├─ Page layout changes while user interacts ├─ Example: ads load, page jumps ├─ Target: <0.1 ├─ Impact: reserve space for images, ads Optimization: ├─ Compress images (WebP format) ├─ Lazy load (load only visible) ├─ Code splitting (split JS into chunks) └─ Cache (CDN, browser cache) ``` ## CDN (Content Delivery Network) ``` Problem: user in Tokyo, server in us-east-1 ├─ Request latency: 100ms ├─ User experience: slow CDN: ├─ Cache static files (JS, CSS, images) globally ├─ User in Tokyo → fetches from Tokyo edge ├─ Latency: 10ms (much better!) Examples: Cloudflare, CloudFront, Fastly Cost: $0.085 per GB (varies) What to cache: ├─ Images: 1 year TTL (versioned in URL) ├─ CSS/JS: 1 day TTL (auto-versioned) ├─ HTML: 5 min TTL (updates frequent) └─ API: don't cache (data changes) ``` ## Accessibility Basics ``` A11y (web accessibility): Keyboard navigation: ├─ Tab key: move between buttons, links ├─ Screen readers: read alt text for images └─ Test: try navigating with keyboard only Alt text: └─ Describes image for screen readers Semantic HTML: ✓ (accessible)
